title: OpenAI and more than 100 organisations call for an AI-powered cyber-defence push
friendlyTitle: AI companies want a faster push to protect important computer systems
summary: An OpenAI-led open letter urges companies, governments and AI labs to accelerate defensive AI, fix high-risk weaknesses and share verified tools and playbooks, with priority for under-resourced critical infrastructure. Its signatories argue that increasingly capable models will expand both attack and defence capacity.
friendlySummary: OpenAI and more than 100 groups say hospitals, water systems and other important services need stronger cyber defence. They want companies and governments to share tools, training and tested fixes.
whyItMatters: For organisations, the practical message is to treat patching, least privilege, strong authentication and AI-generated code review as leadership priorities now. Lower-cost defensive models may widen security coverage, but they need authorised testing, observability and accountable agent identities.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Businesses should fix serious security problems, limit access and check AI-written code now. AI can help defenders, but its actions still need clear rules and records.
